correctness.rationale: The hypotheses are for the smooth complex blow-up of two disjoint triples on distinct lines, with their intersection not a center. Any irreducible plane curve other than the two lines has sum of the six multiplicities at most twice its degree d by Bézout, so its transform has anticanonical degree at least d. Adjunction forces d=1 if that transform is negative, and the only other nonexceptional negative curves are the nine lines between the triples. This proves completeness of the 17-curve list and identifies the two intersecting -2 curves as the only anticanonical degree-zero curves, giving A2 on the weak del Pezzo anticanonical model. Selected -1 curves must be disjoint (a meeting pair has singular principal block); their Schur complement permits one root when its selected-exceptional count is at most one, and both roots when the total of those counts is at most one. The selected cross-lines share a row or a column, with the incident exceptional curves excluded. An independent incidence enumeration of 2^9 times 2^6 times 4 selection cases gave (1,17,100,281,401,255,37), sum 1092 and degree six. The enumeration checks coefficients using the proved curve list, not the classification itself. The frozen support files were inspected, not executed; no Lean verification, external attestation, or formal proof certificate is asserted.
